note: Every member BTK inhibitor cleared rodent collagen-induced arthritis, but in methotrexate- or biologic-inadequate-responder RA only fenebrutinib met its Phase 2 primary endpoint; BMS-986142, poseltinib, evobrutinib, elsubrutinib and TAS5315 missed theirs.
label: Rheumatoid arthritis (BTK)

engagement.model: BTK occupancy probe in CIA mice
engagement.note: Spebrutinib track opener: a fluorescent affinity probe first measured BTK occupancy in CIA mice dosed with ibrutinib, a sibling outside the member list; spebrutinib's own probe followed (Evans 2013).
engagement.short: Probe measures BTK occupancy in mice
engagement.quote: Occupancy of the Btk active site by PCI-32765 was monitored in vitro and in vivo using a fluorescent affinity probe for Btk.

engagement.model: BTK occupancy probe in CIA mice
engagement.note: Spebrutinib (CC-292) occupancy that tracked CIA efficacy in mice was reproduced in healthy volunteers: 2 mg/kg engaged all circulating BTK.
engagement.short: Full BTK occupancy in humans, as in mice
engagement.quote: This first-in-human healthy volunteer trial has demonstrated that a single oral dose of 2 mg/kg CC-292 consistently engaged all circulating Btk protein
engagement.reason: Human occupancy matched the mouse readout
engagement.judgement: The same paper reports the mouse CIA occupancy-efficacy link and the human occupancy, so comparison_stated is true; healthy volunteers count. Patient occupancy later agreed (spebrutinib median 83-88% in RA, Schafer 2020; elsubrutinib 'adequate target engagement', Fleischmann 2022), so no further entry.

dose.note: Fenebrutinib track opener: BTK occupancy tightly tracked efficacy in CIA mice (ibrutinib, a sibling), so blood occupancy or inhibition became the class's exposure target.
dose.short: Occupancy tracks efficacy in CIA mice
dose.quote: Active site occupancy of Btk was tightly correlated with the blockade of BCR signaling and in vivo efficacy.

dose.note: Fenebrutinib doses were set to reach the rat-CIA inhibition target (IC70); 150 mg QD and 200 mg BID beat placebo on ACR50, 50 mg QD did not.
dose.short: Rat-CIA exposure target worked in patients
dose.quote: with the goal of achieving plasma concentrations reaching at least IC70, as this extent of inhibition was correlated with efficacy in a rat collagen-induced arthritis model
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7496340, Europe PMC XML); the subscript in IC70 is rendered inline. Whether patients' measured exposure reached IC70 was not checked in the text.
dose.judgement: The paper states the dose basis but does not itself compare the trial result with the rat model, so comparison_stated is false with Crawford 2018 (rat CIA) as model side. Year is the paper (April 2020): the registry posting of 2019-09-10 gives the result but not the rat-derived target.
dose.magnitude_basis: plasma concentration relative to the rat-CIA IC70

dose.note: Elsubrutinib reached adequate exposure and BTK engagement at every dose yet matched placebo; the rat-CIA occupancy target that predicted efficacy did not hold.
dose.quote: No significant improvements in efficacy measures for elsubrutinib alone (any dose) versus placebo were detected, despite adequate plasma exposure and target engagement.
dose.reason: Target reached; drug failed and was dropped
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction: elsubrutinib reached the rat-CIA occupancy target the model stated (Goess 2019: 'BTK occupancy in disease models correlated with in vivo efficacy'), so dose is same; the efficacy failure is scored in efficacy only. Elsubrutinib's own track opens at Goess 2019 (epub 2018). Year from the paper (April 2022); the registry posting of 2021-05-03 gives the result but not the exposure statement.
dose.magnitude_basis: DAS28-CRP change vs placebo at the model-sufficient occupancy

efficacy.note: BMS-986142 track opener: ibrutinib (a sibling) abolished mouse CIA; every member then went into RA on mouse or rat CIA, BMS-986142 on Gillooly 2017.
efficacy.quote: In mice with collagen-induced arthritis, orally administered PCI-32765 reduced the level of circulating autoantibodies and completely suppressed disease.

efficacy.note: BMS-986142 showed robust efficacy in mouse CIA but missed both co-primary endpoints (ACR20 and ACR70, week 12) in MTX-inadequate responders; the authors call the trial negative.
efficacy.quote: Pre-specified interim analysis resulted in discontinuation of the 350 mg BMS-986142 dose due to elevated liver enzymes and absence of benefit versus placebo. Co-primary endpoints were not met.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the paper; primary-endpoint numbers confirmed in the ClinicalTrials.gov results record (ACR20 30.7% placebo vs 35.6/42.5/30.8%, p=0.52/0.14/0.99).
efficacy.judgement: Co-primary design, both missed, scored a failure as the authors call it. Year is the registry results posting (NCT02638948, 2019-05-28); the tier-1 paper sets the status. Each other member is now its own track (appended below). Not neg: the model's own data showed robust CIA efficacy. Model side Gillooly 2017 mouse CIA/CAIA. Acalabrutinib's RA trial (NCT02387762) posted its registered primary, DAS28-CRP at week 4, with no analysis and no quotable statement, so it stays in patient_trials unscored.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ACR20 response vs placebo at week 12

patient_trials.quote: Registered primary DAS28-CRP at week 4: acalabrutinib + MTX 5.40 vs placebo + MTX 5.05 (registry results record, no statistical analysis posted); no verbatim sentence, so not scored.

efficacy.note: Spebrutinib track opener: BTK bound by CC-292 correlated with its efficacy in mouse CIA.
efficacy.short: Occupancy tracks efficacy in mouse CIA
efficacy.quote: These studies demonstrate the quantity of Btk bound by CC-292 correlates with the efficacy of CC-292 in vitro and in the collagen-induced arthritis model of autoimmune disease.

efficacy.note: Spebrutinib 375 mg/day on background MTX missed its registered primary endpoint, ACR20 at week 4 (41.7% vs 21.7%, P = 0.25), despite 83% median BTK occupancy.
efficacy.quote: Clinical efficacy trended higher in spebrutinib-treated RA patients, with 41.7% (10/24) achieving ≥ 20% improvement in ACR response criteria (ACR20) versus 21.7% (5/23) of placebo patients at week 4 (P = 0.25).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 31721017); online 2019-11-13. NCT01975610 registered primary ACR20 week 4; no registry results posted. An earlier congress abstract was not searched.
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry: spebrutinib is its own track. Paired: the RA paper does not compare with the CIA model, so comparison_stated false with Evans 2013 as model side. Small mechanistic trial (n=47) but ACR20 was its registered primary.

efficacy.note: Poseltinib (HM71224) track opener: improved mouse CIA and prevented joint destruction.
efficacy.quote: Finally, HM71224 improved experimental arthritis and prevented joint destruction in a murine model of CIA.

efficacy.note: Poseltinib missed ACR20 at week 12 at every dose; the sponsor stopped Part B after an interim analysis showed low likelihood of benefit.
efficacy.short: No ACR20 benefit; stopped for futility
efficacy.quote: There was no statistically significant difference in ACR20 response between any dose of poseltinib and placebo at Week 12 (P > 0.05 for all comparisons).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 33323529); online 2020-12-15. Registry results NCT02628028 posted 2019-10-09, the earliest public date.
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry. Background DMARDs were allowed in both arms, so no combination partner. Year is the registry posting. Paired with Park 2016 mouse CIA.

efficacy.note: Fenebrutinib track opener: dose-dependent activity in a rat inflammatory arthritis model.
efficacy.quote: GDC-0853 (29) suppresses B cell- and myeloid cell-mediated components of disease and demonstrates dose-dependent activity in an in vivo rat model of inflammatory arthritis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 29457982); online 2018-02-23.

efficacy.note: Fenebrutinib 150 mg QD and 200 mg BID beat placebo on the primary endpoint, ACR50 at week 12 in MTX-inadequate responders (28% and 35% vs 15%); 50 mg QD did not.
efficacy.quote: In cohort 1, American College of Rheumatology scores (ACR50) at week 12 were similar for fenebrutinib 50 mg once daily and placebo, and higher for fenebrutinib 150 mg once daily (28%) and 200 mg twice daily (35%) than placebo (15%)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 32270926); registry results NCT02833350 posted 2019-09-10, the earliest public date found. The ACR 2019 cohort 2 abstract cites cohort 1 as reported earlier (congress abstract not located).
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry: under per-drug tracks fenebrutinib's success is its own track and is no longer outweighed by another drug's failure. Background MTX in all arms; adalimumab was an active comparator, not a partner. Paired with Crawford 2018 rat arthritis.

efficacy.note: Evobrutinib track opener: robust efficacy in mouse RA models; 80% blood BTK occupancy linked to near-complete disease inhibition.
efficacy.quote: In mouse models of RA and SLE, orally administered evobrutinib displayed robust efficacy, as demonstrated by reduction of disease severity and histological damage.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 30988116); online 2019-04-15.
efficacy.judgement: First public 2019-04-15, before the first scored BTK result in RA (BMS-986142 registry, 2019-05-28); the acalabrutinib registry posting of 2019-03-26 carries no analysis and is not scored, so this is not a retrodiction.

efficacy.note: Evobrutinib missed its primary endpoint, ACR20 at week 12, in MTX-inadequate responders (placebo 49.5%); no dose response.
efficacy.quote: This phase IIb study of evobrutinib in patients with RA with inadequate response to MTX did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint of ACR20 response.
efficacy.confidence_note: ACR Convergence 2020 abstract read in full (Arthritis Rheumatol 2020;72 suppl 10), tiered as a published congress abstract; registry results NCT03233230 posted 2020-09-28. No full trial paper found.
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry; replaces the constructed registry quote with the abstract's verbatim conclusion. Year is the registry posting (2020-09-28), before the abstract's November 2020 presentation. Paired with Haselmayer 2019 mouse arthritis.

efficacy.note: Elsubrutinib (ABBV-105) track opener: inhibited paw swelling and bone destruction in rat CIA.
efficacy.quote: ABBV-105 inhibited antibody responses to thymus-independent and thymus-dependent antigens, paw swelling and bone destruction in rat collagen induced arthritis, and reduced disease in an IFNα-accelerated lupus nephritis model.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 29862859); online 2018-07-23.

efficacy.note: Elsubrutinib alone matched placebo at every dose despite adequate exposure and BTK engagement; the ABBV-599 combination arm's benefit was attributed to upadacitinib.
efficacy.short: No benefit alone at any dose
efficacy.quote: No significant improvements in efficacy measures for elsubrutinib alone (any dose) versus placebo were detected, despite adequate plasma exposure and target engagement.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Lancet Rheumatol paywalled); registry results NCT03682705 posted 2021-05-03, the earliest public date.
efficacy.reason: No benefit alone at any dose
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry. Scored on the elsubrutinib-alone arms; the elsubrutinib + upadacitinib (ABBV-599) arm is a combination whose effect the authors attribute to the JAK inhibitor, noted here and not scored as a BTK success. Paired with Goess 2019 rat CIA.

efficacy.note: TAS5315 track opener: dose-dependently ameliorated paw swelling in established mouse CIA at 0.1 mg/kg (ACR 2017 abstract; full paper 2023).
efficacy.quote: In established mouse CIA model, TAS5315 significantly ameliorated paw swelling in a dose-dependent manner and showed the anti-inflammatory effects in pathological analysis at a dose of 0.1 mg/kg.
efficacy.confidence_note: ACR 2017 abstract read in full (first published 2017-09-18, Arthritis Rheumatol 2017;69 suppl 10); the full paper is Akasaka 2023 PLoS One (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0282117). Earliest public date per rule 6, so not a retrodiction.

efficacy.note: TAS5315 missed its primary endpoint, ACR20 at week 12 in MTX-inadequate Japanese patients (78.9% vs 60.0%, p = 0.053).
efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint was not achieved.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 37217273); online 2023-05-22. NCT03605251 has no posted results; an earlier congress or sponsor release was not found.
efficacy.judgement: Split from the BMS-986142 entry. Background MTX in both arms, no partner. Paired with the ACR 2017 mouse CIA abstract.

safety.note: A 28-day mouse finding (spermatid degeneration) kept men out of the spebrutinib RA trial; no BTK-inhibitor toxicology prediction was ever compared with RA patients.
safety.short: Mouse tox shaped trial, never compared
safety.quote: men were excluded from participating based on a preclinical toxicology finding of maturing spermatid degeneration in a 28-day study in mice
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7021855, Europe PMC XML); quote confirmed verbatim.
safety.judgement: Patient-side harms exist (BMS-986142 350 mg arm stopped for liver enzymes, Conaghan 2023; TAS5315 bleeding in 9 patients over 36 weeks, Takeuchi 2023) but no source found states what the toxicology species predicted for either, so no comparison can be scored. Ibrutinib/acalabrutinib oncology toxicology was not imported.

safety.note: Light-transmission aggregometry on healthy-volunteer and CLL-patient platelets, plus a humanized VWF mouse thrombus model, predicted acalabrutinib impairs platelets less than ibrutinib.
safety.short: Platelet assays predict less bleeding than ibrutinib
safety.quote: acalabrutinib appears to have fewer effects than ibrutinib on platelets in aggregometry assays and in a humanized mouse model of thrombus formation.
safety.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled review text (pharmacology section, study report r2017005). The single-arm MCL data in the same review (hemorrhage 31.5%) has no ibrutinib comparator, so it cannot test a relative prediction.
safety.judgement: The prediction is relative (fewer platelet effects than ibrutinib, a sibling outside the member list), so it opens untested until a head-to-head trial; first use proxied by the review date.
safety.model: Human platelet aggregometry and humanized-mouse thrombus formation (acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib)

safety.note: In CLL acalabrutinib had fewer bleeds than ibrutinib (38.0% vs 51.3%). RA patients were measured for BTK-inhibitor safety, so this imported harm does not score; no RA head-to-head exists.
safety.short: Fewer bleeds than ibrutinib, as predicted
safety.quote: Bleeding events were less frequent with acalabrutinib (n = 101 [38.0%]) versus ibrutinib (n = 135 [51.3%]; Data Supplement).
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8547923). Major bleeding comparable (4.5% vs 5.3%), so agreement is on any-grade bleeding only. Imported from CLL; no RA comparison of the platelet prediction exists.
safety.reason: Not scorable: RA patients set safety
safety.judgement: Imported-harm ruling: a harm seen only in another disease's patients is imported only when this disease has no patient safety data for the class. RA trials of several members measured safety (BMS-986142 liver enzymes, TAS5315 bleeding), so the CLL comparison no longer sets the status; the relative bleeding prediction was never measured in RA. Was same.
safety.magnitude_basis: any-grade bleeding incidence, acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib
safety.population: Previously treated CLL with del(17p) or del(11q) (imported)
safety.model: Human platelet aggregometry and humanized-mouse thrombus formation (acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib)
